scope: A coupling verdict is about typed interfaces, not biology. 'composable' means the declared mapping is dimensionally and scope-consistent; it does not mean the models describe the same organism. 'scenario' results are assumption-level. No Lean theorem here proves biological correspondence.

assumptions.text: glide release speed equals the constraint solver's witness V (the glide model's own default is 1.5 x stall speed)
Notch/Delta lateral-inhibition spacing from a two-cell non-dimensional model sets fin-ray stiffness scale (NO source supports this)

the mean lift-pressure proxy p = 0.5*rho*V^2*CL, built from declared rho, V and CL, is the pressure carried by one fin ray (it is not a measured fin pressure; V is the solver's level-flight-proxy speed)
ray length fraction and tributary width are declared values, not measurements (fin_mechanics example: 1/5 of the semispan, 1/100 m)
the flexural-rigidity range is ASSUMED, not measured or calibrated: no calibrated fin stiffness exists in this repository

not_established: that a real tissue obeys these kinetics
